1	"""The Lux-Marchesi (1999) market model, built from the equations in docs/SPEC.md.
     2	
     3	N traders are in one of three groups:
     4	    fundamentalists  buy when the price is below the fundamental value, sell above it
     5	    optimists        chartists who buy
     6	    pessimists       chartists who sell
     7	Traders switch groups at random, at rates that depend on the crowd (herding), the
     8	price trend and the profits of each strategy. Excess demand (buyers minus sellers)
     9	moves the price one tick at a time. News moves the fundamental value as Gaussian
    10	noise, so any fat tails or volatility clustering must come from the traders.
    11	
    12	Section numbers (sec. 1-5) refer to docs/SPEC.md.
    13	
    14	Policy options (an extension, not part of the paper; SPEC.md "Policy experiments"):
    15	circuit breakers that pause or close trading after a big fall within the day, and
    16	one-off policy surprises that move the fundamental value.
    17	"""
    18	import os
    19	
    20	import numpy as np
    21	
    22	try:
    23	    import numba
    24	except ImportError:                    # still works without numba, just ~50x slower
    25	    numba = None
    26	
    27	# Settings. Every one has a fixed meaning in SPEC.md; rates are per unit of time
    28	# (one unit = one trading day).
    29	SETTINGS = {
    30	    "N": "number of traders",
    31	    "v1": "how often chartists reconsider their mood (sec. 1)",
    32	    "v2": "how often traders reconsider their strategy (sec. 2)",
    33	    "a1": "herding: weight of the majority mood (sec. 1)",
    34	    "a2": "trend following: weight of the price trend (sec. 1)",
    35	    "a3": "sensitivity to profit differences (sec. 2)",
    36	    "s": "discount on fundamentalists' future profits, below 1 (sec. 2)",
    37	    "R": "return on other investments per day; dividend yield r/p_f = R (sec. 2)",
    38	    "tc": "trading volume of one chartist (sec. 3)",
    39	    "gamma": "reaction strength of one fundamentalist (sec. 3)",
    40	    "beta": "price speed: relative price change per day per unit of excess demand (sec. 3)",
    41	    "sigma_mu": "standard deviation of the noise in excess demand (sec. 3)",
    42	    "sigma_eps": "daily standard deviation of the news (sec. 4)",
    43	    "tick": "size of one price tick, as a fraction of the price (sec. 3)",
    44	    "dt": "time step, as a fraction of a day (sec. 5)",
    45	    "floor": "minimum number of chartists and of fundamentalists (sec. 5)",
    46	}
    47	
    48	# Parameter set I as remembered from Lux & Marchesi (2000), UNVERIFIED (SPEC.md).
    49	# T_c = N tc = 10 and T_f = N gamma = 5.
    50	SET_I = dict(N=500, v1=3.0, v2=2.0, a1=0.6, a2=0.2, a3=0.5, s=0.75, R=0.0004,
    51	             tc=0.02, gamma=0.01, beta=6.0, sigma_mu=0.05, sigma_eps=0.005,
    52	             tick=0.001, dt=0.01, floor=4)
    53	
    54	TREND_WINDOW = 0.1     # dp/dt is measured over the last 0.1 day (= 10 steps of 0.01) [S]
    55	REFERENCE_DT = 0.01    # the time step of Lux & Marchesi's own simulations [S]
    56	U_CAP = 30.0           # cap on the exponents U, so exp(U) cannot overflow
    57	MAX_GAP = 1.0          # a runaway: the price more than e = 2.7x away from its value...
    58	MAX_DAYS = 250         # ...for a whole year of trading days in a row,
    59	HARD_GAP = 20.0        # or ever more than e^20 (5 hundred million) times away
    60	START_CHARTISTS = 0.1  # share of chartists at the start, split evenly into the two moods
    61	MIN_DT, MIN_TICK, MAX_N = 1e-4, 1e-12, 10**7   # limits of what the computer can do sensibly
    62	MAX_TICKS = 1e15       # ticks in one step beyond this = the price has left any sensible range
    63	# US market-wide circuit breakers since 2013 (NYSE Rule 7.12, formerly Rule 80B;
    64	# SEC-approved): a 15-minute pause when the S&P 500 is 7% or 13% below the previous
    65	# close, but only before 3:25 pm (minute 355 of the day); closed for the day at 20%
    66	# at any time.
    67	US_BREAKERS = dict(levels=(0.07, 0.13, 0.20), halt_minutes=15, last_pause_minute=355)
    68	MINUTES_PER_DAY = 390  # 9:30 to 16:00
    69	
    70	
    71	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ checks
    72	
    73	class RunawayError(RuntimeError):
    74	    """The price left its value for good (all traders became chartists)."""
    75	
    76	    def __init__(self, message, day):
    77	        super().__init__(message)
    78	        self.day = day
    79	
    80	
    81	def check(p):
    82	    """Raise ValueError unless p has exactly the known settings with sensible values."""
    83	    if not isinstance(p, dict):
    84	        raise ValueError(f"settings must be a dict, got {type(p).__name__}")
    85	    unknown, missing = set(p) - set(SETTINGS), set(SETTINGS) - set(p)
    86	    if unknown or missing:
    87	        raise ValueError(f"unknown settings {sorted(unknown)}, missing settings {sorted(missing)}")
    88	    for k, v in p.items():
    89	        if isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(v, (int, float, np.number)) \
    90	                or not np.isfinite(v):
    91	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be a finite number, got {v!r}")
    92	        if v < 0:
    93	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must not be negative, got {v}")
    94	    # floor 0 would let the chartists die out: then opinion x = (n+ - n-)/n_c divides by 0
    95	    for k in ("N", "v1", "v2", "beta", "tick", "dt", "floor"):
    96	        if p[k] <= 0:
    97	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be above 0, got {p[k]}")
    98	    for k in ("N", "floor"):
    99	        if int(p[k]) != p[k]:
   100	            raise ValueError(f"setting {k} must be a whole number, got {p[k]}")
   101	    if not p["s"] < 1:
   102	        raise ValueError(f"s must be below 1 (the paper's discount factor), got {p['s']}")
   103	    if not p["tick"] < 1:
   104	        raise ValueError(f"tick must be below 1 (a fraction of the price), got {p['tick']}")
   105	    steps = round(1 / p["dt"])
   106	    if abs(steps * p["dt"] - 1) > 1e-9:
   107	        raise ValueError(f"dt must split one day into whole steps (0.01, 0.005, ...), got {p['dt']}")
   108	    w = TREND_WINDOW / p["dt"]
   109	    if w < 1 - 1e-9 or abs(w - round(w)) > 1e-9:
   110	        raise ValueError(f"dt must split the trend window ({TREND_WINDOW} day) into whole steps "
   111	                         f"(0.01, 0.005, ...), got {p['dt']}")
   112	    if p["dt"] < MIN_DT:
   113	        raise ValueError(f"dt must be at least {MIN_DT} (smaller steps take too long and too much memory), got {p['dt']}")
   114	    if p["tick"] < MIN_TICK:
   115	        raise ValueError(f"tick must be at least {MIN_TICK} (smaller ticks round to 0), got {p['tick']}")
   116	    if p["N"] > MAX_N:
   117	        raise ValueError(f"N must be at most {MAX_N:,}, got {p['N']}")
   118	    if p["N"] < 4 * p["floor"]:
   119	        raise ValueError(f"N={p['N']} is too small for floor={p['floor']}: need N >= 4*floor")
   120	
   121	
   122	STEP_LIMIT = 2.0       # above this, the time step itself makes the price blow up
   123	
   124	
   125	def step_pull(p):
   126	    """How much of a mispricing the fundamentalists remove in ONE time step, at most
   127	    (all N of them): beta * N * gamma * dt (from SPEC eq. 25 with ED_f = n_f gamma gap).
   128	    Below 1 the price moves part of the way back to its value each step; between 1
   129	    and 2 it overshoots but the swings shrink; at STEP_LIMIT (2) or more every step
   130	    overshoots by more than the last, and the run explodes even without chartists.
   131	    That is a flaw of stepping through time, not a bubble."""
   132	    return p["beta"] * p["N"] * p["gamma"] * p["dt"]
   133	
   134	
   135	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ one time step
   136	
   137	def _leave(g, n, rate_a, rate_b, dt):
   138	    """Of n traders each leaving at rate_a (to A) or rate_b (to B) per day, how many
   139	    go to A and to B within dt. Exact for constant rates: a trader leaves with
   140	    probability 1 - exp(-(rate_a + rate_b) dt), then picks A with chance
   141	    rate_a / (rate_a + rate_b)."""
   142	    total = rate_a + rate_b
   143	    if n <= 0 or total <= 0.0:
   144	        return 0, 0
   145	    k = g.binomial(n, 1.0 - np.exp(-total * dt))
   146	    to_a = g.binomial(k, rate_a / total)
   147	    return to_a, k - to_a
   148	
   149	
   150	def _cap(u):
   151	    return min(U_CAP, max(-U_CAP, u))
   152	
   153	
   154	def _simulate(g, days, steps, chartists, N, v1, v2, a1, a2, a3, s, R, tc, gamma,
   155	              beta, sigma_mu, sigma_eps, tick, floor, n_plus, n_minus, max_gap, max_days,
   156	              hard_gap, cb1, cb2, cb3, halt_steps, pause_end, shock):
   157	    """The simulation loop (see SPEC.md). Returns per-day log price, log value,
   158	    chartist share and opinion at each day's close, the circuit-breaker level of
   159	    each day, and the number of days completed (fewer than `days` if the price ran
   160	    away: |log price - log value| above max_gap for max_days days in a row, or ever
   161	    above hard_gap).
   162	    Circuit breakers: 0 > cb1 > cb2 > cb3 are log falls from the previous close
   163	    (-inf = off). Falling to cb1 or cb2 within the first pause_end steps of the day

    70	        raise ValueError("need at least one history")
    71	    keys = list(target)
    72	    v = np.array([[f[k] for k in keys] for f in fingerprints])
    73	    spread = np.where(v.std(axis=0) > 0, v.std(axis=0), 1.0)
    74	    miss = np.mean(((v - np.array([target[k] for k in keys])) / spread) ** 2, axis=1)
    75	    return int(np.argsort(miss)[(len(miss) - 1) // 2])

1	"""Policy experiments (an extension, not part of the paper; SPEC.md "Policy experiments").
     2	
     3	1. Circuit breakers: do the US rules (pause at -7% and -13%, close at -20%) make
     4	   crashes rarer, or only spread them out? Each seed is run twice, without and with
     5	   breakers, so the two runs share the same randomness until the first halt.
     6	2. A policy surprise (like an unexpected rate hike): the fundamental value drops
     7	   once by 10%. Does the price fall by 10%, or does the crowd make it overshoot?
     8	
     9	The breaker levels are rescaled by the model's volatility relative to the
    10	S&P 500's, so "7%" means the same number of typical days in both.
    11	"""
    12	import numpy as np
    13	
    14	from . import model
    15	from .experiments import BURN, worst_fall
    16	
    17	
    18	def scaled_breakers(model_sd, market_sd, rules=model.US_BREAKERS):
    19	    """The breaker rules with every level multiplied by model_sd / market_sd."""
    20	    if not (model_sd > 0 and market_sd > 0):
    21	        raise ValueError(f"both volatilities must be above 0, got {model_sd}, {market_sd}")
    22	    scale = model_sd / market_sd
    23	    levels = tuple(x * scale for x in rules["levels"])
    24	    if not levels[-1] < 1:
    25	        raise ValueError(f"the model is {scale:.1f}x as volatile as the market: "
    26	                         f"the scaled levels {levels} reach 100%")
    27	    return dict(rules, levels=levels), scale       # every other rule is kept as it is
    28	
    29	
    30	def crash_measures(r, crash_level):
    31	    """How bad the crashes of one history are: the worst 1-, 5- and 20-day falls
    32	    (positive log returns), and the number of days that fell more than crash_level."""
    33	    return dict(worst_1d=worst_fall(r, 1), worst_5d=worst_fall(r, 5),
    34	                worst_20d=worst_fall(r, 20),
    35	                crash_days=int(np.sum(np.asarray(r) <= np.log(1 - crash_level))))
    36	
    37	
    38	EVENT_DAYS = (1, 5, 20)            # horizons of the first-halt comparison
    39	
    40	
    41	def _breaker_pair(args):
    42	    p, seed, days, rules = args
    43	    try:
    44	        off = model.simulate(p, days + BURN, seed=seed)
    45	        on = model.simulate(p, days + BURN, seed=seed, breakers=rules)
    46	    except model.RunawayError:
    47	        return None
    48	    level = rules["levels"][0]
    49	    out = dict(off=crash_measures(off["r"][BURN:], level), on=crash_measures(on["r"][BURN:], level))
    50	    out["on"]["halt_days"] = int(np.sum(on["halts"][BURN:] > 0))
    51	    out["on"]["closed_days"] = int(np.sum(on["halts"][BURN:] == 3))
    52	    # The two runs use identical random numbers up to the first halt, so that day is
    53	    # a clean comparison: how far did the price fall from the previous close
    54	    # within 1, 5 and 20 days, with and without the breaker?
    55	    # (The first halt of the whole run, warm-up included: after any halt the runs
    56	    # differ. It must leave max(EVENT_DAYS) days to measure.)
    57	    fired = np.flatnonzero(on["halts"] > 0)
    58	    out["event"] = None
    59	    if fired.size and fired[0] + max(EVENT_DAYS) <= days + BURN:
    60	        d = int(fired[0])
    61	        out["event"] = {side: {k: float(run["lp"][d + k] - run["lp"][d]) for k in EVENT_DAYS}
    62	                        for side, run in (("off", off), ("on", on))}
    63	    return out
    64	
    65	
    66	def breaker_experiment(pool, p, seeds, days, rules):
    67	    """Paired runs without and with breakers, one pair per seed. Returns
    68	    (whole, events, runaways):
    69	        whole   {"off"|"on": {measure: array}}: crash_measures of every whole history
    70	        events  {"off"|"on": {k: array}}: at each history's first halt, the log change
    71	                from the previous close after k days (EVENT_DAYS), for histories with a halt
    72	        runaways  number of seeds whose history ran away (left out)"""
    73	    rows = pool.map(_breaker_pair, [(p, int(s), int(days), rules) for s in seeds])
    74	    ok = [r for r in rows if r is not None]
    75	    if not ok:
    76	        return None, None, len(rows)
    77	    whole = {side: {k: np.array([r[side][k] for r in ok]) for k in ok[0][side]}
    78	             for side in ("off", "on")}
    79	    ev = [r["event"] for r in ok if r["event"] is not None]
    80	    events = {side: {k: np.array([e[side][k] for e in ev]) for k in EVENT_DAYS}
    81	              for side in ("off", "on")}
    82	    return whole, events, len(rows) - len(ok)
    83	
    84	
    85	def _surprise_one(args):
    86	    p, seed, size, horizon = args
    87	    day = BURN + int(np.random.default_rng(seed).integers(0, 5000))   # when the surprise hits
    88	    try:
    89	        o = model.simulate(p, day + horizon, seed=seed, shocks={day: size})
    90	        calm = model.simulate(p, day + horizon, seed=seed)    # placebo: no surprise
    91	    except model.RunawayError:
    92	        return None
    93	
    94	    def ratio(run):
    95	        # The mispricing (log price - log value) just before the surprise is gap[day].
    96	        # A price that followed the value exactly would keep it. The fall of the
    97	        # price in units of the surprise is 1 minus the change in mispricing since.
    98	        gap = run["lp"] - run["lf"]
    99	        return 1.0 - (gap[day + 1:day + horizon + 1] - gap[day]) / -np.log1p(size)
   100	
   101	    hit, placebo = ratio(o), ratio(calm) - 1.0      # placebo: ordinary wobble only
   102	    return dict(chartists=float(o["z"][day]), peak=float(hit.max()), end=float(hit[-1]),
   103	                placebo_peak=float(placebo.max()))
   104	
   105	
   106	def surprise_experiment(pool, p, seeds, size=-0.10, horizon=10):
   107	    """One surprise per seed, on a random day after the warm-up: the value drops
   108	    once by `size`. For each history: the chartist share the day before, and the
   109	    price's fall in units of the surprise over the next `horizon` days (1 = the
   110	    price fell exactly as much as the value, 1.2 = it overshot by 20%): `peak` = the
   111	    largest, `end` = after `horizon` days. News is still on, so the value keeps
   112	    moving too; the measure follows the price relative to the value.
   113	    `placebo_peak`: the same peak in the same history without the surprise, minus 1
   114	    (how much of `peak - 1` the ordinary wobble of the mispricing gives by itself).
   115	    Returns ({name: array} over the seeds that did not run away, how many did)."""
   116	    if not (-1 < size < 0):
   117	        raise ValueError(f"size must be a fall between -1 and 0, got {size}")
   118	    rows = list(pool.map(_surprise_one, [(p, int(s), size, horizon) for s in seeds]))
   119	    ok = [r for r in rows if r is not None]
   120	    return {k: np.array([r[k] for r in ok]) for k in ("chartists", "peak", "end", "placebo_peak")}, \
   121	        len(rows) - len(ok)
   122	
   123	
   124	def median_overshoot(peak, placebo_peak, draws=2000, seed=0):
   125	    """The overshoot caused by the surprise, history by history: the median of
   126	    peak - (placebo_peak + 1) (each history minus its own placebo), with a 95%
   127	    bootstrap interval (resampling the histories). Returns (median, low, high).
   128	    (The difference of the two medians, as read off the table, is only a shortcut.)"""
   129	    d = np.asarray(peak, dtype=float) - (np.asarray(placebo_peak, dtype=float) + 1)
   130	    if d.size < 2:
   131	        raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 histories, got {d.size}")
   132	    g = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   133	    meds = np.median(d[g.integers(0, d.size, (draws, d.size))], axis=1)
   134	    return float(np.median(d)), float(np.quantile(meds, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(meds, 0.975))
   135	
   136	
   137	def paired_difference(off, on, draws=2000, seed=0):
   138	    """Mean of on - off over paired runs, with a 95% bootstrap interval (resampling
   139	    the pairs). Returns (mean, low, high)."""
   140	    d = np.asarray(on, dtype=float) - np.asarray(off, dtype=float)
   141	    if d.size < 2:
   142	        raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 pairs, got {d.size}")
   143	    g = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   144	    means = d[g.integers(0, d.size, (draws, d.size))].mean(axis=1)
   145	    return float(d.mean()), float(np.quantile(means, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(means, 0.975))
     1	"""Political parties (an extension, not part of the paper): is the market different
     2	under Democratic and Republican presidents, and could a model with no politics in it
     3	produce a gap that big by luck?
     4	
     5	The "presidential puzzle" (Santa-Clara & Valkanov 2003, J. Finance 58: 1841-1872):
     6	1927-1998, US stocks returned about 9 points a year more under Democratic presidents,
     7	with no matching difference in risk. Pastor & Veronesi (2020, J. Political Economy
     8	128: 4011-4045) found it continued, and argue the party is not the cause: when
     9	investors are fearful, voters pick Democrats, and fearful markets later pay more.
    10	
    11	Here the model is the yardstick. It has no politics (its news is the same bell curve
    12	every day), so any "party gap" in a model history is pure chance. Cutting many model
    13	histories at the real inauguration dates shows how big a gap chance alone gives.
    14	"""
    15	import numpy as np
    16	import pandas as pd
    17	
    18	from . import experiments, market_data, stats
    19	
    20	# The party of the president from each date on (inauguration days; public record).
    21	PRESIDENTS = [
    22	    ("1923-08-02", "R", "Coolidge"), ("1929-03-04", "R", "Hoover"),
    23	    ("1933-03-04", "D", "Roosevelt"), ("1945-04-12", "D", "Truman"),
    24	    ("1953-01-20", "R", "Eisenhower"), ("1961-01-20", "D", "Kennedy"),
    25	    ("1963-11-22", "D", "Johnson"), ("1969-01-20", "R", "Nixon"),
    26	    ("1974-08-09", "R", "Ford"), ("1977-01-20", "D", "Carter"),
    27	    ("1981-01-20", "R", "Reagan"), ("1989-01-20", "R", "Bush"),
    28	    ("1993-01-20", "D", "Clinton"), ("2001-01-20", "R", "Bush"),
    29	    ("2009-01-20", "D", "Obama"), ("2017-01-20", "R", "Trump"),
    30	    ("2021-01-20", "D", "Biden"), ("2025-01-20", "R", "Trump"),
    31	]
    32	DAYS_PER_YEAR = 252
    33	CRASH_SD = 4.0          # a "crash day": a fall of more than 4 standard deviations
    34	
    35	
    36	def democrat(dates):
    37	    """True on each date with a Democratic president (dates: anything pandas reads)."""
    38	    dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates)
    39	    first = pd.Timestamp(PRESIDENTS[0][0])
    40	    if len(dates) and dates.min() < first:
    41	        raise ValueError(f"dates before {first.date()} are not covered")
    42	    starts = pd.DatetimeIndex([d for d, _, _ in PRESIDENTS])
    43	    i = starts.searchsorted(dates, side="right") - 1   # the latest inauguration on or before
    44	    return np.array([PRESIDENTS[j][1] == "D" for j in i])
    45	
    46	
    47	def switches(dates):
    48	    """Day indexes where the party changes, and the party from there on."""
    49	    dem = democrat(dates)
    50	    at = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(dem.astype(int))) + 1
    51	    return np.concatenate([[0], at]), np.where(dem[np.concatenate([[0], at])], "D", "R")
    52	
    53	
    54	def party_gap(r, dem):
    55	    """How returns differ between Democratic (dem True) and Republican days, in units
    56	    of the whole series' daily standard deviation so that a real market and a model of
    57	    different volatility can be compared:
    58	        mean      (mean D - mean R) per year, in daily sds (x DAYS_PER_YEAR)
    59	        vol       sd on D days / sd on R days (1 = the same)
    60	        kurtosis  excess kurtosis on D days minus on R days
    61	        crashes   crash days (below -CRASH_SD sds) per 1,000 days, D minus R"""
    62	    r = stats._returns(r)
    63	    dem = np.asarray(dem, dtype=bool)
    64	    if dem.shape != r.shape:
    65	        raise ValueError(f"need one party per return: {dem.shape} vs {r.shape}")
    66	    if dem.sum() < 500 or (~dem).sum() < 500:
    67	        raise ValueError("need at least 500 days under each party")
    68	    sd = r.std()
    69	    d, g = r[dem], r[~dem]
    70	    crash = lambda x: 1000 * np.mean(x < r.mean() - CRASH_SD * sd)
    71	    return dict(mean=float((d.mean() - g.mean()) / sd * DAYS_PER_YEAR),
    72	                vol=float(d.std() / g.std()),
    73	                kurtosis=float(stats.kurtosis(d) - stats.kurtosis(g)),
    74	                crashes=float(crash(d) - crash(g)))
    75	
    76	
    77	MEASURES = {
    78	    "mean": "return gap per year, D minus R (daily sds)",
    79	    "vol": "volatility, D / R",
    80	    "kurtosis": "fat tails (excess kurtosis), D minus R",
    81	    "crashes": "crash days per 1,000, D minus R",
    82	}
    83	
    84	
    85	def shifted_gaps(r, dem, step=63, margin=DAYS_PER_YEAR):
    86	    """party_gap of the SAME returns with the party calendar slid along by every multiple
    87	    of `step` days (63 = a quarter), wrapping around, at least `margin` days from the
    88	    real calendar. A fake calendar keeps the real terms' lengths and the market's own
    89	    calm and wild spells, so the gaps it gives are what luck alone does with this market."""
    90	    dem = np.asarray(dem, dtype=bool)
    91	    shifts = range(margin, len(dem) - margin + 1, step)
    92	    if len(shifts) < 20:
    93	        raise ValueError(f"too few shifts ({len(shifts)}): need a longer series or a smaller step")
    94	    return [party_gap(r, np.roll(dem, k)) for k in shifts]
    95	
    96	
    97	def compare(market, p, seeds, pool=None, days=None):
    98	    """The real gap, and two yardsticks for luck, each with the real market's percentile:
    99	    the model's gaps at the same dates (one per history that did not run away), and the
   100	    market's own returns with the party calendar shifted (shifted_gaps).
   101	    days: use only the market's last `days` days (None = all; small for quick tests)."""
   102	    r = market_data.returns(market)
   103	    r = r if days is None else r.iloc[-int(days):]
   104	    dem = democrat(r.index)
   105	    real = party_gap(r.values, dem)
   106	    runs = [h["r"] for h in experiments.histories(p, seeds, len(r), pool=pool) if h is not None]
   107	    nulls = {"model": [party_gap(x, dem) for x in runs],
   108	             "shifted": shifted_gaps(r.values, dem)}
   109	    pct = {name: {k: experiments.percentile(real[k], [s[k] for s in null]) for k in MEASURES}
   110	           for name, null in nulls.items()}
   111	    return r, dem, real, nulls, pct
   112	
   113	
   114	def terms(dates, min_days=20):
   115	    """Each presidency's stretch of `dates` (sorted trading days): a list of dicts with
   116	    name, party and the day indexes a:b (b not included). Terms with fewer than
   117	    min_days trading days in `dates` (e.g. before the data start) are left out."""
   118	    dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates)
   119	    starts = [pd.Timestamp(d) for d, _, _ in PRESIDENTS] + [pd.Timestamp("2100-01-01")]
   120	    out = []
   121	    for i, (_, party, name) in enumerate(PRESIDENTS):
   122	        a, b = int(dates.searchsorted(starts[i])), int(dates.searchsorted(starts[i + 1]))
   123	        if b - a >= min_days:
   124	            out.append(dict(name=name, party=party, a=a, b=b, start=dates[a], end=dates[b - 1]))
   125	    return out
     1	"""Real-market data, loaded with checks so a bad file fails loudly.
     2	
     3	All files come from data/download_market_data.py and end on the same day (2026-10-30).
     4	
     5	Markets (daily closes from Yahoo Finance):
     6	    spx       S&P 500, 1950-today   (the calibration target)
     7	    spx_1928  S&P 500, 1928-today   (adds the 1929 crash and the Great Depression;
     8	              Yahoo omits Saturday sessions before 1952, and early prices are coarser)
     9	    ndx       Nasdaq-100, 1985-today
    10	Stocks: data/stocks/<TICKER>.csv, large S&P 500 companies whose market beta
    11	(how much they move per 1% market move, 2005-2025) is between 0.9 and 1.1.
    12	"""
    13	from pathlib import Path
    14	
    15	import numpy as np
    16	import pandas as pd
    17	
    18	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent      # the project folder
    19	DATA = ROOT / "data"
    20	SPX = DATA / "sp500_daily.csv"
    21	MARKETS = {"spx": SPX, "spx_1928": DATA / "sp500_daily_from_1928.csv", "ndx": DATA / "nasdaq100_daily.csv"}
    22	STOCKS = DATA / "stocks"
    23	BLACK_MONDAY = pd.Timestamp("1987-10-19")
    24	
    25	
    26	def load_prices(path):
    27	    """Daily closes from a CSV with Date and Close columns, checked: sorted,
    28	    unique dates, positive prices."""
    29	    path = Path(path)
    30	    if not path.exists():
    31	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{path} not found. Download every data file with: "
    32	                                f"python3 data/download_market_data.py")
    33	    df = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=["Date"], index_col="Date")
    34	    close = df["Close"]
    35	    if close.isna().any() or not (close > 0).all():
    36	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: every Close price must be positive (found NaN or <= 0)")
    37	    if not df.index.is_monotonic_increasing or df.index.duplicated().any():
    38	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: dates must be sorted and unique")
    39	    return df
    40	
    41	
    42	def load_spx(path=SPX):
    43	    """Daily S&P 500 closes since 1950 (the calibration target)."""
    44	    return load_prices(path)
    45	
    46	
    47	def _log_returns(df):
    48	    return np.log(df["Close"]).diff().dropna()
    49	
    50	
    51	def spx_returns(spx=None):
    52	    """Daily log returns of the S&P 500, as a Series indexed by the later date."""
    53	    return _log_returns(load_spx() if spx is None else spx)
    54	
    55	
    56	def returns(market):
    57	    """Daily log returns of a named market: 'spx', 'spx_1928' or 'ndx'."""
    58	    if market not in MARKETS:
    59	        raise ValueError(f"unknown market {market!r}; choose from {sorted(MARKETS)}")
    60	    return _log_returns(load_prices(MARKETS[market]))
    61	
    62	
    63	def stock_tickers():
    64	    """Tickers of the saved market-beta-matched stocks."""
    65	    return sorted(pd.read_csv(STOCKS / "market_beta.csv")["ticker"])
    66	
    67	
    68	def stock_returns(ticker):
    69	    """Daily log returns of one saved stock (split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted,
    70	    the same as the index files; see data/stocks/README.md)."""
    71	    if ticker not in stock_tickers():
    72	        raise ValueError(f"unknown stock {ticker!r}; saved stocks: {stock_tickers()}")
    73	    return _log_returns(load_prices(STOCKS / f"{ticker}.csv")).rename(ticker)
    74	
    75	
    76	def black_monday(returns):
    77	    """Log return on 1987-10-19 (the record one-day crash)."""
    78	    if BLACK_MONDAY not in returns.index:
    79	        raise ValueError("the S&P 500 data has no 1987-10-19 (Black Monday); re-download it")
    80	    return float(returns.loc[BLACK_MONDAY])
     1	"""Drawing helpers shared by main.py, make_figures.py and (later) the web app.
     2	
     3	One palette everywhere, checked for colour-blind safety (the dataviz validator:
     4	blue, orange and aqua pass as a set of three in light mode):
     5	    real market data         INK (near-black)
     6	    S&P-calibrated model     BLUE
     7	    paper-matched model      ORANGE
     8	    no chartists / news      AQUA
     9	Aqua is low-contrast on white, so it is always labelled (legend or text), never
    10	identified by colour alone.
    11	"""
    12	from math import erfc
    13	from pathlib import Path
    14	
    15	import matplotlib
    16	
    17	matplotlib.use("Agg")
    18	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    19	import numpy as np
    20	
    21	from . import stats
    22	
    23	INK, SECOND, MUTED, GRID = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781", "#e1e0d9"
    24	BLUE, ORANGE, AQUA = "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"

    38	
    39	
    40	def style():

    42	
    43	
    44	def save(fig, path, title, caption):

    57	def ccdf(ax, r, label, color, points=None, **kw):
    58	    """Log-log tail plot: share of days whose |standardized return| exceeds x.
    59	    With `points`, draw about that many markers, spaced evenly on the log x axis and
    60	    each on a real data point (the largest move always included), as in Lux &
    61	    Marchesi's Fig 2; otherwise draw every point as a line."""
    62	    z, cc = stats.ccdf(r)
    63	    keep = z > 0
    64	    z, cc = z[keep], cc[keep]
    65	    if points:
    66	        grid = np.geomspace(z[0], z[-1], points)
    67	        i = np.unique(np.append(np.minimum(np.searchsorted(z, grid), len(z) - 1), len(z) - 1))
    68	        z, cc = z[i], cc[i]
    69	        kw = dict(dict(ls="none", marker="o", ms=4), **kw)
    70	    ax.loglog(z, cc, color=color, label=label, **kw)

    73	def gaussian_ccdf(ax, label="bell curve N(0,1)", ls="--"):
    74	    g = np.geomspace(0.05, 6, 200)
    75	    # share of a bell curve beyond +-x: erfc(x / sqrt 2). (math.erfc, not scipy: scipy
    76	    # takes about half a second to load, in every worker process)
    77	    ax.loglog(g, [erfc(x / np.sqrt(2)) for x in g], ls, color=MUTED, lw=1.2, label=label)

    80	def power_law(ax, x0, y0, slope, x1, label=None, color=MUTED, **kw):
    81	    """Reference line y = y0 (x / x0)^slope from x0 to x1: a straight line of the given
    82	    slope on log-log axes (a tail exponent is minus the slope; H is the slope)."""
    83	    x = np.array([x0, x1])
    84	    return ax.loglog(x, y0 * (x / x0) ** slope, color=color, label=label, **dict(dict(ls="--", lw=1.1), **kw))[0]

    87	def dfa(ax, x, scales, label, color, marker="o", shift=1.0, fit_ls="-"):
    88	    """DFA fluctuation F(n) vs window n (log-log), with the fitted slope H in the label.
    89	    Returns (H, the first window, its fitted F) so a reference slope can start there."""
    90	    s, F = stats.dfa(x, scales)
    91	    coef = np.polyfit(np.log(s), np.log(F), 1)
    92	    ax.loglog(s, F * shift, marker, color=color, ms=4.5, lw=0, label=f"{label}: H = {coef[0]:.2f}")
    93	    fit = np.exp(np.polyval(coef, np.log(s))) * shift
    94	    ax.loglog(s, fit, fit_ls, color=color, lw=1.0)
    95	    return coef[0], s[0], fit[0]

     2	
     3	1. Circuit breakers: do the US rules (pause at -7% and -13%, close at -20%) make
     4	   crashes rarer, or only spread them out? Each seed is run twice, without and with
     5	   breakers, so the two runs share the same randomness until the first halt.
     6	2. A policy surprise (like an unexpected rate hike): the fundamental value drops
     7	   once by 10%. Does the price fall by 10%, or does the crowd make it overshoot?
     8	
     9	The breaker levels are rescaled by the model's volatility relative to the
    10	S&P 500's, so "7%" means the same number of typical days in both.
    11	"""
    12	import numpy as np
    13	
    14	from . import model
    15	from .experiments import BURN, worst_fall

    18	def scaled_breakers(model_sd, market_sd, rules=model.US_BREAKERS):
    19	    """The breaker rules with every level multiplied by model_sd / market_sd."""
    20	    if not (model_sd > 0 and market_sd > 0):
    21	        raise ValueError(f"both volatilities must be above 0, got {model_sd}, {market_sd}")
    22	    scale = model_sd / market_sd
    23	    levels = tuple(x * scale for x in rules["levels"])
    24	    if not levels[-1] < 1:
    25	        raise ValueError(f"the model is {scale:.1f}x as volatile as the market: "
    26	                         f"the scaled levels {levels} reach 100%")
    27	    return dict(rules, levels=levels), scale       # every other rule is kept as it is
    28	
    29	
    30	def crash_measures(r, crash_level):
    31	    """How bad the crashes of one history are: the worst 1-, 5- and 20-day falls
    32	    (positive log returns), and the number of days that fell more than crash_level."""
    33	    return dict(worst_1d=worst_fall(r, 1), worst_5d=worst_fall(r, 5),
    34	                worst_20d=worst_fall(r, 20),
    35	                crash_days=int(np.sum(np.asarray(r) <= np.log(1 - crash_level))))
    36	
    37	
    38	EVENT_DAYS = (1, 5, 20)            # horizons of the first-halt comparison
    39	
    40	
    41	def _breaker_pair(args):
    42	    p, seed, days, rules = args
    43	    try:
    44	        off = model.simulate(p, days + BURN, seed=seed)
    45	        on = model.simulate(p, days + BURN, seed=seed, breakers=rules)
    46	    except model.RunawayError:
    47	        return None
    48	    level = rules["levels"][0]
    49	    out = dict(off=crash_measures(off["r"][BURN:], level), on=crash_measures(on["r"][BURN:], level))
    50	    out["on"]["halt_days"] = int(np.sum(on["halts"][BURN:] > 0))
    51	    out["on"]["closed_days"] = int(np.sum(on["halts"][BURN:] == 3))
    52	    # The two runs use identical random numbers up to the first halt, so that day is
    53	    # a clean comparison: how far did the price fall from the previous close
    54	    # within 1, 5 and 20 days, with and without the breaker?
    55	    # (The first halt of the whole run, warm-up included: after any halt the runs
    56	    # differ. It must leave max(EVENT_DAYS) days to measure.)
    57	    fired = np.flatnonzero(on["halts"] > 0)
    58	    out["event"] = None
    59	    if fired.size and fired[0] + max(EVENT_DAYS) <= days + BURN:
    60	        d = int(fired[0])
    61	        out["event"] = {side: {k: float(run["lp"][d + k] - run["lp"][d]) for k in EVENT_DAYS}
    62	                        for side, run in (("off", off), ("on", on))}
    63	    return out

    66	def breaker_experiment(pool, p, seeds, days, rules):
    67	    """Paired runs without and with breakers, one pair per seed. Returns
    68	    (whole, events, runaways):
    69	        whole   {"off"|"on": {measure: array}}: crash_measures of every whole history
    70	        events  {"off"|"on": {k: array}}: at each history's first halt, the log change
    71	                from the previous close after k days (EVENT_DAYS), for histories with a halt
    72	        runaways  number of seeds whose history ran away (left out)"""
    73	    rows = pool.map(_breaker_pair, [(p, int(s), int(days), rules) for s in seeds])
    74	    ok = [r for r in rows if r is not None]
    75	    if not ok:
    76	        return None, None, len(rows)
    77	    whole = {side: {k: np.array([r[side][k] for r in ok]) for k in ok[0][side]}
    78	             for side in ("off", "on")}
    79	    ev = [r["event"] for r in ok if r["event"] is not None]
    80	    events = {side: {k: np.array([e[side][k] for e in ev]) for k in EVENT_DAYS}
    81	              for side in ("off", "on")}
    82	    return whole, events, len(rows) - len(ok)

    85	def _surprise_one(args):
    86	    p, seed, size, horizon = args
    87	    day = BURN + int(np.random.default_rng(seed).integers(0, 5000))   # when the surprise hits
    88	    try:
    89	        o = model.simulate(p, day + horizon, seed=seed, shocks={day: size})
    90	        calm = model.simulate(p, day + horizon, seed=seed)    # placebo: no surprise
    91	    except model.RunawayError:
    92	        return None
    93	
    94	    def ratio(run):
    95	        # The mispricing (log price - log value) just before the surprise is gap[day].
    96	        # A price that followed the value exactly would keep it. The fall of the
    97	        # price in units of the surprise is 1 minus the change in mispricing since.
    98	        gap = run["lp"] - run["lf"]
    99	        return 1.0 - (gap[day + 1:day + horizon + 1] - gap[day]) / -np.log1p(size)
   100	
   101	    hit, placebo = ratio(o), ratio(calm) - 1.0      # placebo: ordinary wobble only
   102	    return dict(chartists=float(o["z"][day]), peak=float(hit.max()), end=float(hit[-1]),
   103	                placebo_peak=float(placebo.max()))

   106	def surprise_experiment(pool, p, seeds, size=-0.10, horizon=10):
   107	    """One surprise per seed, on a random day after the warm-up: the value drops
   108	    once by `size`. For each history: the chartist share the day before, and the
   109	    price's fall in units of the surprise over the next `horizon` days (1 = the
   110	    price fell exactly as much as the value, 1.2 = it overshot by 20%): `peak` = the
   111	    largest, `end` = after `horizon` days. News is still on, so the value keeps
   112	    moving too; the measure follows the price relative to the value.
   113	    `placebo_peak`: the same peak in the same history without the surprise, minus 1
   114	    (how much of `peak - 1` the ordinary wobble of the mispricing gives by itself).
   115	    Returns ({name: array} over the seeds that did not run away, how many did)."""
   116	    if not (-1 < size < 0):
   117	        raise ValueError(f"size must be a fall between -1 and 0, got {size}")
   118	    rows = list(pool.map(_surprise_one, [(p, int(s), size, horizon) for s in seeds]))
   119	    ok = [r for r in rows if r is not None]
   120	    return {k: np.array([r[k] for r in ok]) for k in ("chartists", "peak", "end", "placebo_peak")}, \
   121	        len(rows) - len(ok)

   124	def median_overshoot(peak, placebo_peak, draws=2000, seed=0):
   125	    """The overshoot caused by the surprise, history by history: the median of
   126	    peak - (placebo_peak + 1) (each history minus its own placebo), with a 95%
   127	    bootstrap interval (resampling the histories). Returns (median, low, high).
   128	    (The difference of the two medians, as read off the table, is only a shortcut.)"""
   129	    d = np.asarray(peak, dtype=float) - (np.asarray(placebo_peak, dtype=float) + 1)
   130	    if d.size < 2:
   131	        raise ValueError(f"need at least 2 histories, got {d.size}")
   132	    g = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   133	    meds = np.median(d[g.integers(0, d.size, (draws, d.size))], axis=1)
   134	    return float(np.median(d)), float(np.quantile(meds, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(meds, 0.975))

   137	def paired_difference(off, on, draws=2000, seed=0):
   138	    """Mean of on - off over paired runs, with a 95% bootstrap interval (resampling
   139	    the pairs). Returns (mean, low, high)."""
   140	    d = np.asarray(on, dtype=float) - np.asarray(off, dtype=float)
   141	    if d.size < 2:

   143	    g = np.random.default_rng(seed)
   144	    means = d[g.integers(0, d.size, (draws, d.size))].mean(axis=1)

     1	"""Political parties (an extension, not part of the paper): is the market different
     2	under Democratic and Republican presidents, and could a model with no politics in it
     3	produce a gap that big by luck?
     4	
     5	The "presidential puzzle" (Santa-Clara & Valkanov 2003, J. Finance 58: 1841-1872):
     6	1927-1998, US stocks returned about 9 points a year more under Democratic presidents,
     7	with no matching difference in risk. Pastor & Veronesi (2020, J. Political Economy
     8	128: 4011-4045) found it continued, and argue the party is not the cause: when
     9	investors are fearful, voters pick Democrats, and fearful markets later pay more.
    10	
    11	Here the model is the yardstick. It has no politics (its news is the same bell curve
    12	every day), so any "party gap" in a model history is pure chance. Cutting many model
    13	histories at the real inauguration dates shows how big a gap chance alone gives.
    14	"""
    15	import numpy as np
    16	import pandas as pd
    17	
    18	from . import experiments, market_data, stats
    19	
    20	# The party of the president from each date on (inauguration days; public record).
    21	PRESIDENTS = [
    22	    ("1923-08-02", "R", "Coolidge"), ("1929-03-04", "R", "Hoover"),
    23	    ("1933-03-04", "D", "Roosevelt"), ("1945-04-12", "D", "Truman"),
    24	    ("1953-01-20", "R", "Eisenhower"), ("1961-01-20", "D", "Kennedy"),
    25	    ("1963-11-22", "D", "Johnson"), ("1969-01-20", "R", "Nixon"),
    26	    ("1974-08-09", "R", "Ford"), ("1977-01-20", "D", "Carter"),
    27	    ("1981-01-20", "R", "Reagan"), ("1989-01-20", "R", "Bush"),
    28	    ("1993-01-20", "D", "Clinton"), ("2001-01-20", "R", "Bush"),
    29	    ("2009-01-20", "D", "Obama"), ("2017-01-20", "R", "Trump"),
    30	    ("2021-01-20", "D", "Biden"), ("2025-01-20", "R", "Trump"),
    31	]
    32	DAYS_PER_YEAR = 252
    33	CRASH_SD = 4.0          # a "crash day": a fall of more than 4 standard deviations
    34	
    35	
    36	def democrat(dates):
    37	    """True on each date with a Democratic president (dates: anything pandas reads)."""
    38	    dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates)
    39	    first = pd.Timestamp(PRESIDENTS[0][0])
    40	    if len(dates) and dates.min() < first:
    41	        raise ValueError(f"dates before {first.date()} are not covered")
    42	    starts = pd.DatetimeIndex([d for d, _, _ in PRESIDENTS])
    43	    i = starts.searchsorted(dates, side="right") - 1   # the latest inauguration on or before
    44	    return np.array([PRESIDENTS[j][1] == "D" for j in i])
    45	
    46	
    47	def switches(dates):
    48	    """Day indexes where the party changes, and the party from there on."""
    49	    dem = democrat(dates)
    50	    at = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(dem.astype(int))) + 1
    51	    return np.concatenate([[0], at]), np.where(dem[np.concatenate([[0], at])], "D", "R")
    52	
    53	
    54	def party_gap(r, dem):
    55	    """How returns differ between Democratic (dem True) and Republican days, in units
    56	    of the whole series' daily standard deviation so that a real market and a model of
    57	    different volatility can be compared:
    58	        mean      (mean D - mean R) per year, in daily sds (x DAYS_PER_YEAR)
    59	        vol       sd on D days / sd on R days (1 = the same)
    60	        kurtosis  excess kurtosis on D days minus on R days
    61	        crashes   crash days (below -CRASH_SD sds) per 1,000 days, D minus R"""
    62	    r = stats._returns(r)
    63	    dem = np.asarray(dem, dtype=bool)
    64	    if dem.shape != r.shape:
    65	        raise ValueError(f"need one party per return: {dem.shape} vs {r.shape}")
    66	    if dem.sum() < 500 or (~dem).sum() < 500:
    67	        raise ValueError("need at least 500 days under each party")
    68	    sd = r.std()
    69	    d, g = r[dem], r[~dem]
    70	    crash = lambda x: 1000 * np.mean(x < r.mean() - CRASH_SD * sd)
    71	    return dict(mean=float((d.mean() - g.mean()) / sd * DAYS_PER_YEAR),
    72	                vol=float(d.std() / g.std()),
    73	                kurtosis=float(stats.kurtosis(d) - stats.kurtosis(g)),
    74	                crashes=float(crash(d) - crash(g)))
    75	
    76	
    77	MEASURES = {
    78	    "mean": "return gap per year, D minus R (daily sds)",
    79	    "vol": "volatility, D / R",
    80	    "kurtosis": "fat tails (excess kurtosis), D minus R",
    81	    "crashes": "crash days per 1,000, D minus R",
    82	}

    85	def shifted_gaps(r, dem, step=63, margin=DAYS_PER_YEAR):
    86	    """party_gap of the SAME returns with the party calendar slid along by every multiple
    87	    of `step` days (63 = a quarter), wrapping around, at least `margin` days from the
    88	    real calendar. A fake calendar keeps the real terms' lengths and the market's own
    89	    calm and wild spells, so the gaps it gives are what luck alone does with this market."""
    90	    dem = np.asarray(dem, dtype=bool)
    91	    shifts = range(margin, len(dem) - margin + 1, step)
    92	    if len(shifts) < 20:
    93	        raise ValueError(f"too few shifts ({len(shifts)}): need a longer series or a smaller step")
    94	    return [party_gap(r, np.roll(dem, k)) for k in shifts]

    97	def compare(market, p, seeds, pool=None, days=None):
    98	    """The real gap, and two yardsticks for luck, each with the real market's percentile:
    99	    the model's gaps at the same dates (one per history that did not run away), and the
   100	    market's own returns with the party calendar shifted (shifted_gaps).
   101	    days: use only the market's last `days` days (None = all; small for quick tests)."""
   102	    r = market_data.returns(market)
   103	    r = r if days is None else r.iloc[-int(days):]
   104	    dem = democrat(r.index)
   105	    real = party_gap(r.values, dem)
   106	    runs = [h["r"] for h in experiments.histories(p, seeds, len(r), pool=pool) if h is not None]
   107	    nulls = {"model": [party_gap(x, dem) for x in runs],
   108	             "shifted": shifted_gaps(r.values, dem)}
   109	    pct = {name: {k: experiments.percentile(real[k], [s[k] for s in null]) for k in MEASURES}
   110	           for name, null in nulls.items()}
   111	    return r, dem, real, nulls, pct
   112	
   113	
   114	def terms(dates, min_days=20):
   115	    """Each presidency's stretch of `dates` (sorted trading days): a list of dicts with
   116	    name, party and the day indexes a:b (b not included). Terms with fewer than
   117	    min_days trading days in `dates` (e.g. before the data start) are left out."""
   118	    dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates)
   119	    starts = [pd.Timestamp(d) for d, _, _ in PRESIDENTS] + [pd.Timestamp("2100-01-01")]
   120	    out = []
   121	    for i, (_, party, name) in enumerate(PRESIDENTS):
   122	        a, b = int(dates.searchsorted(starts[i])), int(dates.searchsorted(starts[i + 1]))
   123	        if b - a >= min_days:
   124	            out.append(dict(name=name, party=party, a=a, b=b, start=dates[a], end=dates[b - 1]))
   125	    return out

1	"""Fit the model's settings to target numbers (docs/SPEC.md, "Parameters").

     3	Two fits, by one method:
     4	    paper   reproduce Lux & Marchesi (1999)'s published numbers (alpha 2.64,

    10	STABILITY_SEEDS and keep the best-scoring one among those with the fewest runaways

    12	uses the same TRAIN_SEEDS (so two settings are compared on the same luck); checks
    13	of a fitted model must use other seeds (HELD_OUT_SEEDS).

   281	def checkpointed(pool, fn, jobs, path):
   282	    """pool.map(fn, jobs), but each result is saved as one JSON line in `path` as
   283	    soon as it is done, and results already in the file are not recomputed. So a
   284	    fit that is stopped (a flat battery) loses at most the jobs that were running.
   285	    Every result must be JSON-friendly; lists come back as tuples."""
   286	    path = Path(path)
   287	    done = {}
   288	    if path.exists():
   289	        for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
   290	            try:
   291	                rec = json.loads(line)
   292	            except json.JSONDecodeError:              # a line cut off mid-write
   293	                continue
   294	            done[rec["i"]] = tuple(rec["out"]) if isinstance(rec["out"], list) else rec["out"]
   295	    todo = [i for i in range(len(jobs)) if i not in done]
   296	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   297	    with path.open("a") as f:
   298	        if path.stat().st_size and not path.read_bytes().endswith(b"\n"):

   300	        for i, out in zip(todo, pool.imap(fn, [jobs[i] for i in todo])):
   301	            f.write(json.dumps({"i": i, "out": out}) + "\n")
   302	            f.flush()
   303	            done[i] = tuple(out) if isinstance(out, list) else out
   304	    return [done[i] for i in range(len(jobs))]

   307	def run(kind, draws=1200, keep=8, iters=150, workers=8, checkpoint_dir=CHECKPOINT_DIR):

   309	    returns (loss, settings, runaways). Progress is saved in checkpoint_dir, so
   310	    running the same command again after a stop continues where it was; the
   311	    checkpoint files are removed once the fit has finished."""

   313	    t = time.time()
   314	    tag = Path(checkpoint_dir) / f"{kind}_draws{draws}_keep{keep}_iters{iters}"
   315	    with Pool(workers) as pool:
   316	        scored = checkpointed(pool, fit.score_draw, list(range(draws)), f"{tag}_search.jsonl")
   317	        scored.sort(key=lambda d: d[0])
   318	        print(f"{kind}: {draws} random settings in {time.time() - t:.0f}s; "
   319	              f"best loss {scored[0][0]:.2f}; runaways {sum(s >= RUNAWAY_LOSS for s, _ in scored)}",
   320	              flush=True)
   321	        refined = checkpointed(pool, _refine, [(fit, p, iters, f"{tag}_refine{j}_scores.jsonl")
   322	                                               for j, (_, p) in enumerate(scored[:keep])],
   323	                               f"{tag}_refine.jsonl")
   324	        print(f"{kind}: refined {keep} in {time.time() - t:.0f}s total; stability screen:", flush=True)
   325	        bad, loss, p = screen(pool, refined)[0]
   326	    print(f"{kind}: chose loss {loss:.3f} ({bad} runaways) after {time.time() - t:.0f}s")
   327	    for part in ["search", "refine"] + [f"refine{j}_scores" for j in range(keep)]:
   328	        Path(f"{tag}_{part}.jsonl").unlink(missing_ok=True)

   215	    def __init__(self, fn, path):
   216	        self.fn, self.path, self.cache = fn, Path(path), {}
   217	        # a line cut off mid-write would glue onto the next one: end it first
   218	        if self.path.exists() and self.path.stat().st_size \
   219	                and not self.path.read_bytes().endswith(b"\n"):
   220	            with self.path.open("a") as f:
   221	                f.write("\n")

   224	                try:

   226	                except json.JSONDecodeError:          # a line cut off mid-write
   227	                    continue
   228	                self.cache[tuple(rec["v"])] = rec["loss"]

   230	    def __call__(self, v):

   233	            self.cache[key] = float(self.fn(np.array(key)))
   234	            self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   235	            with self.path.open("a") as f:
   236	                f.write(json.dumps({"v": list(key), "loss": self.cache[key]}) + "\n")

   242	    fit, p, iters = args[:3]
   243	    loss = fit.loss_of_vector if len(args) < 4 else SavedLoss(fit.loss_of_vector, args[3])
   244	    res = minimize(loss, to_vector(p, fit.ranges), method="Nelder-Mead",
   245	                   options=dict(maxfev=iters, xatol=1e-3, fatol=1e-3))

   249	def _runs_away(args):

   258	def runaways(pool, p, seeds=STABILITY_SEEDS, days=STABILITY_DAYS):

   260	    rule (more than e away from the value for MAX_DAYS days in a row)."""
   261	    return int(sum(pool.map(_runs_away, [(p, int(s), int(days)) for s in seeds])))

   264	def screen(pool, candidates, seeds=STABILITY_SEEDS, days=STABILITY_DAYS):
   265	    """Stability screen: sort (loss, settings) candidates by (runaways, loss), so the
   266	    best fit among the never-runaway ones comes first. Returns (runaways, loss, p)."""
   267	    # one pool.map over every (candidate, seed), so no worker waits between candidates
   268	    jobs = [(p, int(s), int(days)) for _, p in candidates for s in seeds]
   269	    ran_away = pool.map(_runs_away, jobs, chunksize=1)
   270	    counts = [int(sum(ran_away[i * len(seeds):(i + 1) * len(seeds)])) for i in range(len(candidates))]
   271	    out = sorted(((bad, loss, p) for bad, (loss, p) in zip(counts, candidates)),
   272	                 key=lambda c: (c[0], c[1]))
   273	    for bad, loss, _ in out:

   281	def checkpointed(pool, fn, jobs, path):
   282	    """pool.map(fn, jobs), but each result is saved as one JSON line in `path` as
   283	    soon as it is done, and results already in the file are not recomputed. So a
   284	    fit that is stopped (a flat battery) loses at most the jobs that were running.
   285	    Every result must be JSON-friendly; lists come back as tuples."""
   286	    path = Path(path)

   288	    if path.exists():

   292	            except json.JSONDecodeError:              # a line cut off mid-write
   293	                continue
   294	            done[rec["i"]] = tuple(rec["out"]) if isinstance(rec["out"], list) else rec["out"]

   297	    with path.open("a") as f:

   318	        print(f"{kind}: {draws} random settings in {time.time() - t:.0f}s; "
   319	              f"best loss {scored[0][0]:.2f}; runaways {sum(s >= RUNAWAY_LOSS for s, _ in scored)}",
   320	              flush=True)

.............................................................."""Can herding explain market crashes? The Lux-Marchesi model vs the S&P 500.

Run:  python3 scripts/main.py    -> prints the comparison table, saves figures/fig00_quick_check_sp500_vs_model.png
Uses the S&P-calibrated settings (settings/sp500_calibrated.json) and held-out seeds only.
"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))   # the project folder, so `herding` imports
import numpy as np

from herding import calibrate, experiments, plots, stats
from herding import market_data as data

FIGURES = data.ROOT / "figures"
SEEDS = calibrate.HELD_OUT_SEEDS[:20]        # never used by the calibration


def table(target, sims):
    """One line per measure: S&P value, model median with its 5-95% range, and the
    S&P's percentile among the model histories (flagged if outside 5-95)."""
    lines = [f"{'measure':<11}{'S&P 500':>10}{'model median (5-95% range)':>34}{'S&P pct':>9}"]
    for k in target:
        v = np.array([f[k] for f in sims])
        lo, med, hi = np.percentile(v, [5, 50, 95])
        pct = experiments.percentile(target[k], v)
        flag = "" if 5 <= pct <= 95 else "  <- unusual"
        lines.append(f"{k:<11}{target[k]:>10.4f}{med:>12.4f} ({lo:8.4f} to {hi:8.4f})"
                     f"{pct:>8.0f}%{flag}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(p=None, out=FIGURES / "fig00_quick_check_sp500_vs_model.png", seeds=SEEDS, days=None):
    p = calibrate.load("spx") if p is None else p
    real = data.spx_returns()
    bm = data.black_monday(real)
    real = real.values
    days = len(real) if days is None else days
    print(f"S&P 500: {len(real):,} daily returns, 1950-2026")
    print(f"Black Monday 1987: {np.expm1(bm):.1%} in one day = "
          f"{abs(bm) / real.std():.1f} standard deviations")
    with experiments.Pool() as pool:
        runs = experiments.histories(p, seeds, days, keep=("r", "z"), pool=pool)
        base = experiments.returns(p, seeds[:1], days, chartists=False, pool=pool)[0]
    ok = [h for h in runs if h is not None]
    ok_seeds = [s for s, h in zip(seeds, runs) if h is not None]
    if len(ok) < len(runs):
        print(f"warning: {len(runs) - len(ok)} of {len(runs)} histories ran away")
    target = stats.fingerprint(real)
    sims = [stats.fingerprint(h["r"]) for h in ok]
    print(f"\n{len(ok)} held-out model histories of {days:,} days each:")
    print(table(target, sims))
    print(f"\nno chartists: kurtosis {stats.kurtosis(base):.3f} (bell curve = 0)")
    i = experiments.typical(sims, target)
    plots.comparison(real, ok[i]["r"], ok[i]["z"], base, out)
    print(f"saved {out} (the typical history: seed {ok_seeds[i]})")
    return real, ok[i]["r"], base


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Every model check uses held-out seeds that neither fit ever saw.

import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))   # the project folder, so `herding` imports
from multiprocessing import Pool

import numpy as np

from herding import calibrate, experiments, kirman, market_data, model, plots, policy, politics, stats
from herding.plots import (BLUE, BLUE_LIGHT, GRID, INK, MUTED, NEWS, ORANGE,
                           ORANGE_LIGHT, PAPER_MODEL, REAL, SECOND, SPX_MODEL, plt)

FIG = market_data.ROOT / "figures"

LONG = 100_000                                 # days in a long run (the paper's Figs 2-3)

LABEL.update(sd="daily sd", kurtosis="kurtosis", alpha_hill="tail α (Hill)",
             alpha_reg="tail α (paper's fit)", ac_r_1="next-day corr.",
             ac_abs_1="clustering, 1 day", ac_abs_50="clustering, 50 days",
             H="H of returns", H_abs="H of |returns|", kurt_5="kurtosis, 5 days",
             kurt_25="kurtosis, 25 days")


def shade(hex_color, amount):
    """Mix a colour with white: amount 0 = the colour, 1 = white."""
    c = np.array([int(hex_color[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5)]) / 255
    return tuple(c + (1 - c) * amount)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ Fig 1
def fig1_snapshot(paper_run, spx_run, spx, path=FIG / "fig01_price_follows_value.png", days=4000):
    """The paper's Fig 1: price tracks its value, but returns are wilder than the news.
    Paper conventions: 4,000 days; price solid, value dotted and shifted down for
    visibility; output (b) and input (c) on the same y range. Added: the chartist
    share (d) and the last 4,000 days of the real S&P 500 (right)."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(4, 3, figsize=(17, 10), sharex=True)
    t = np.arange(days + 1)
    for col, (run, color, name) in enumerate([(paper_run, PAPER_MODEL, "paper-matched model"),
                                              (spx_run, SPX_MODEL, "S&P-calibrated model")]):
        lp, lf, z = run["lp"][:days + 1], run["lf"][:days + 1], run["z"][:days + 1]
        a = ax[0, col]
        price = 100 * np.exp(lp - lp[0])
        gap = 5 * np.ceil(0.1 * np.ptp(price))        # the paper's vertical shift, in whole 5s
        a.plot(t, price, color=color, lw=1.0, label="price p")
        a.plot(t, 100 * np.exp(lf - lp[0]) - gap, ":", color=INK, lw=1.0,
               label=f"fundamental value p_f (drawn {gap:.0f} lower)")
        a.set_title(f"a. Price and value ({name})")
        lo_, hi_ = min(price.min(), (100 * np.exp(lf - lp[0]) - gap).min()), price.max()
        a.set_ylim(lo_ - 0.05 * (hi_ - lo_), hi_ + 0.4 * (hi_ - lo_))     # room for the legend
        a.legend(loc="upper left", frameon=True, facecolor="white", edgecolor=GRID, framealpha=0.9)
        r, eps = np.diff(lp), np.diff(lf)
        lim = 1.1 * max(np.abs(r).max(), np.abs(eps).max())
        ax[1, col].plot(t[1:], r, color=color, lw=0.4)
        ax[1, col].set_title("b. The output: daily returns ln p_t − ln p_t−1")
        ax[2, col].plot(t[1:], eps, color=NEWS, lw=0.4)
        ax[2, col].set_title("c. The input: news ε_t = ln p_f,t − ln p_f,t−1 (Gaussian)")
        for a, x in ((ax[1, col], r), (ax[2, col], eps)):
            a.set_ylim(-lim, lim)
            a.text(0.01, 0.92, f"kurtosis {stats.kurtosis(x):.1f}", transform=a.transAxes,
                   fontsize=8.5, color=INK, va="top")

def table(target, sims):
    """One line per measure: S&P value, model median with its 5-95% range, and the
    S&P's percentile among the model histories (flagged if outside 5-95)."""
    lines = [f"{'measure':<11}{'S&P 500':>10}{'model median (5-95% range)':>34}{'S&P pct':>9}"]
    for k in target:

        lo, med, hi = np.percentile(v, [5, 50, 95])
        pct = experiments.percentile(target[k], v)
        flag = "" if 5 <= pct <= 95 else "  <- unusual"
        lines.append(f"{k:<11}{target[k]:>10.4f}{med:>12.4f} ({lo:8.4f} to {hi:8.4f})"
                     f"{pct:>8.0f}%{flag}")

    ok_seeds = [s for s, h in zip(seeds, runs) if h is not None]

# Analysis scripts

Each script answers one question about the rebuilt model and prints the numbers
quoted in `figures/RESULTS.md` and `KEY_POINTS.md`. They use the fitted settings
in `settings/` and held-out seeds only. Run from the project folder, e.g.
`python3 scripts/analysis/long_run_stability.py`.

| Script | Question |
|---|---|
| `efficient_market_claims.py` | Lux & Marchesi's efficient-market claims: price = value on average, no persistent mispricing, volatility vs chartist share |
| `bounce_back_after_big_days.py` | After a big move, does the price bounce back (like the S&P) or keep sliding? |
| `president_terms.py` | Term by term: which presidencies can the politics-free model explain? (Fig 12b) |
| `president_party_gap.py` | Is the S&P different under Democratic and Republican presidents, beyond luck? (Fig 12) |
| `time_step_check.py` | Do results change with the time step dt? (`spx` or `paper`; the paper-matched ones do) |
| `long_run_stability.py` | How often do the fitted settings run away over 100,000 days? |

Earlier exploration scripts (for the model before the November 2026 rebuild)

def close(a, b, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-12):
    return bool(np.allclose(a, b, rtol=rtol, atol=atol, equal_nan=True))


def outcome(fn, *a, **kw):
    """('ok', value) | ('ValueError', msg) | (other exception name, msg)."""
    try:
        return "ok", fn(*a, **kw)
    except ValueError as e:
        return "ValueError", str(e)
    except Exception as e:                         # noqa: BLE001
        return type(e).__name__, str(e)


# ====================================================================== model.check
def oracle_check(p):
    """The rules of model.check, written out again from SPEC.md / the docstring."""
    if not isinstance(p, dict) or set(p) != set(model.SETTINGS):
        return False
    for v in p.values():
        if isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(v, (int, float, np.integer, np.floating)):
            return False
        if not math.isfinite(float(v)) or v < 0:
            return False
    for k in ("N", "v1", "v2", "beta", "tick", "dt", "floor"):
        if not p[k] > 0:
            return False
    if p["N"] != int(p["N"]) or p["floor"] != int(p["floor"]):
        return False
    if not (p["s"] < 1 and p["tick"] < 1):
        return False
    spd = 1 / p["dt"]
    if abs(spd - round(spd)) * p["dt"] > 1e-9:
        return False
    w = 0.1 / p["dt"]
    if w < 1 - 1e-9 or abs(w - round(w)) > 1e-9:
        return False
    if p["dt"] < 1e-4 or p["tick"] < 1e-12 or p["N"] > 10 ** 7 or p["N"] < 4 * p["floor"]:
        return False
    return True

         np.float32(0.5), np.int64(7), np.complex128(1 + 0j), 1j, np.float64(2.0), 0.5, 1, 2, 3.5]
GOOD_DT = [0.1, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025, 0.002, 0.001, 0.0005, 0.0002, 0.0001]

                     dt=float(rng.choice(GOOD_DT + [0.03, 0.3, 1.0, 0.0001 / 2, 1 / 3])),
                     tick=float(10 ** rng.uniform(-13, 0.1)), s=float(rng.uniform(0, 1.2)))

def sim_case(args):
    seed, = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    res = []
    rec = lambda name, ok, ex=None: res.append((name, bool(ok), None if ok else repr(ex)[:600]))
    p = random_settings(rng)

    chart = bool(rng.random() < 0.85)

        return res
    except Exception as e:                          # noqa: BLE001
        rec("simulate returns or raises RunawayError (nothing else)", False,
            (p, days, kw, type(e).__name__, str(e), traceback.format_exc()[-400:]))
        return res
    rec("simulate returns or raises RunawayError (nothing else)", True)
    N, fl = p["N"], p["floor"]
    rec("series lengths are days+1 (closes) and days (returns, halts)",
        all(len(o[k]) == days + 1 for k in ("lp", "lf", "z", "x")) and len(o["r"]) == days and len(o["halts"]) == days)
    rec("everything finite", all(np.all(np.isfinite(o[k])) for k in ("lp", "lf", "z", "x", "r")), p)
    rec("starts at price = value = 1 (log 0)", o["lp"][0] == 0 and o["lf"][0] == 0)
    rec("r is the day-to-day change of log price", np.array_equal(o["r"], np.diff(o["lp"])))
    rec("same seed -> identical run", all(np.array_equal(o[k], v) for k, v in
                                           model.simulate(p, days, **kw).items()))
    nc = o["z"] * N
    rec("chartist counts are whole numbers", close(nc, np.round(nc), atol=1e-6), nc[:5])
    if chart:
        rec("floor: at least `floor` chartists and fundamentalists every day",
            np.all(np.round(nc) >= fl) and np.all(N - np.round(nc) >= fl), (N, fl, nc.min(), nc.max()))
        rec("opinion x is between -1 and 1", np.all(np.abs(o["x"]) <= 1 + 1e-12))
        npl = np.round(nc * (1 + o["x"]) / 2)
        rec("optimist counts are whole numbers", close(npl, nc * (1 + o["x"]) / 2, atol=1e-6))
    else:
        rec("no chartists: z = 0 and x = 0 all along", np.all(o["z"] == 0) and np.all(o["x"] == 0))
    rec("halts only take values 0-3", set(np.unique(o["halts"])) <= {0, 1, 2, 3})
    if brk is None:
        rec("no breakers -> no halts", np.all(o["halts"] == 0))
    else:
        fall = o["r"]
        l1, l2, l3 = (np.log(1 - x) for x in brk["levels"])
        d3 = o["halts"] == 3
        rec("a day closed by breaker level 3 closes at least that far down", np.all(fall[d3] <= l3 + 1e-12),
            (fall[d3], l3))
        if "last_pause_minute" not in brk:

                np.all(fall[o["halts"] == 0] > l1 - 1e-12), (fall[o["halts"] == 0].min(), l1))

            close(np.diff(o["lf"]), want, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12), (np.diff(o["lf"])[:5], want[:5]))

def rand_returns(rng):
    n_ = int(rng.choice([1, 2, 3, 11, 30, 100, 501, 2000, 5000]))
    kind = rng.integers(0, 6)
    if kind == 0:
        r = rng.standard_normal(n_)
    elif kind == 1:

# ====================================================================== kirman
def transition_matrix(N, eps, delta):
    P = np.zeros((N + 1, N + 1))
    for k in range(N + 1):
        u = (N - k) / N * (eps + (1 - delta) * k / (N - 1))
        d = k / N * (eps + (1 - delta) * (N - k) / (N - 1))
        if k < N:
            P[k, k + 1] = u
        if k > 0:
            P[k, k - 1] = d
        P[k, k] = 1 - u - d
    return P


def fuzz_kirman(rng):
    for _ in range(n(2000)):
        N = int(rng.integers(2, 60))
        eps = float(10 ** rng.uniform(-4, 0))
        delta = float(rng.uniform(0, 1))
        P = transition_matrix(N, eps, delta)
        valid = bool(np.all(P >= -1e-12))
        kind, pi = outcome(kirman.stationary, N, eps, delta)
        record("kirman.stationary accepts exactly the parameters whose chances are valid",
               (kind == "ok") == valid or (kind == "ValueError" and "underflow" in pi), (N, eps, delta, kind, pi))
        if kind != "ok":
            continue
        record("kirman.stationary sums to 1, nothing negative", close(pi.sum(), 1) and np.all(pi >= 0))
        record("kirman.stationary is symmetric (A and B identical)", close(pi, pi[::-1], rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-12))
        record("kirman.stationary is unchanged by one step of the chain (pi P = pi)",
               close(pi @ P, pi, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-12), (N, eps, delta))
        crit = (1 - delta) / (N - 1)
        if eps < 0.5 * crit and N >= 10:
            record("herding regime (eps << (1-delta)/(N-1)): the extremes are the most likely",
                   pi[0] > pi[N // 2], (N, eps, delta))
        if eps > 2 * crit and N >= 10:
            record("no-herding regime (eps >> (1-delta)/(N-1)): 50/50 is the most likely",
                   pi[N // 2] > pi[0], (N, eps, delta))
    for _ in range(n(600)):
        N = int(rng.integers(2, 40))
        eps = float(10 ** rng.uniform(-3, -0.5))
        delta = float(rng.uniform(0.3, 1))
        if outcome(kirman.check, N, eps, delta)[0] != "ok":
            continue
        k0 = int(rng.integers(0, N + 1))
        steps = int(rng.integers(0, 3000))
        k = kirman.simulate(N, eps, delta, steps, seed=int(rng.integers(1e9)), k0=k0)
        record("kirman.simulate: length steps+1, starts at k0, stays in 0..N, moves by at most 1",
               len(k) == steps + 1 and k[0] == k0 and k.min() >= 0 and k.max() <= N
               and (steps == 0 or np.abs(np.diff(k)).max() <= 1))
    # long run frequencies match the exact answer (chi-square-ish, generous)
    for i in range(n(30)):
        N, eps, delta = int(rng.integers(5, 20)), float(rng.uniform(0.02, 0.2)), 0.5
        if outcome(kirman.check, N, eps, delta)[0] != "ok":
            continue
        k = kirman.simulate(N, eps, delta, 400_000, seed=i)
        emp = np.bincount(k, minlength=N + 1) / len(k)
        pi = kirman.stationary(N, eps, delta)
        record("kirman.simulate visits each k as often as the exact answer says (total variation < 0.05)",
               0.5 * np.abs(emp - pi).sum() < 0.05, (N, eps, 0.5 * np.abs(emp - pi).sum()))
    for args in [(1, 0.1, 0.5), (2.5, 0.1, 0.5), (np.nan, 0.1, 0.5), (10, 0, 0.5), (10, 1.5, 0.5), (10, 0.1, -0.1),
                 (10, 0.1, 1.1), (10, np.nan, 0.5), (10, 0.1, np.nan), (True, 0.1, 0.5), ("10", 0.1, 0.5)]:
        kind, val = outcome(kirman.check, *args)
        record("kirman.check rejects bad parameters with ValueError", kind == "ValueError", (args, kind, val))
    for kw in [dict(steps=-1), dict(steps=1.5), dict(steps=5, k0=-1), dict(steps=5, k0=11), dict(steps=5, k0=True),
               dict(steps=5, k0=2.5), dict(steps=np.nan)]:
        kind, val = outcome(kirman.simulate, 10, 0.1, 0.5, **kw)
        record("kirman.simulate rejects bad steps/k0 with ValueError", kind == "ValueError", (kw, kind, val))

"""Large randomized test sweep of the herding package (an audit, not part of tests/).

Every check compares the code with an answer worked out independently (brute force,
scipy, or the rule written out again by hand), on random inputs including edge cases.
Run from the project folder:  python3 scratch/test_audit/fuzz.py [scale]
Writes scratch/test_audit/fuzz_results.json (counts, and up to 5 failing examples per check).

import json
import math
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import traceback
from collections import defaultdict
from multiprocessing import Pool
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import scipy.stats as sps

SCALE = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1.0
OUT = Path(__file__).with_name("fuzz_results.json")
PASS = defaultdict(int)
FAIL = defaultdict(list)
NFAIL = defaultdict(int)


def record(name, ok, example=None):
    if ok:
        PASS[name] += 1
    else:
        NFAIL[name] += 1
        if len(FAIL[name]) < 5:
            FAIL[name].append(repr(example)[:600])


def n(k):
    return max(1, int(k * SCALE))


def close(a, b, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-12):
    return bool(np.allclose(a, b, rtol=rtol, atol=atol, equal_nan=True))


def outcome(fn, *a, **kw):
    """('ok', value) | ('ValueError', msg) | (other exception name, msg)."""
    try:
        return "ok", fn(*a, **kw)
    except ValueError as e:
        return "ValueError", str(e)
    except Exception as e:                         # noqa: BLE001
        return type(e).__name__, str(e)


# ====================================================================== model.check
def oracle_check(p):
    """The rules of model.check, written out again from SPEC.md / the docstring."""
    if not isinstance(p, dict) or set(p) != set(model.SETTINGS):
        return False
    for v in p.values():
        if isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) or not isinstance(v, (int, float, np.integer, np.floating)):
            return False
        if not math.isfinite(float(v)) or v < 0:
            return False
    for k in ("N", "v1", "v2", "beta", "tick", "dt", "floor"):
        if not p[k] > 0:
            return False
    if p["N"] != int(p["N"]) or p["floor"] != int(p["floor"]):
        return False
    if not (p["s"] < 1 and p["tick"] < 1):
        return False
    spd = 1 / p["dt"]
    if abs(spd - round(spd)) * p["dt"] > 1e-9:
        return False
    w = 0.1 / p["dt"]
    if w < 1 - 1e-9 or abs(w - round(w)) > 1e-9:
        return False
    if p["dt"] < 1e-4 or p["tick"] < 1e-12 or p["N"] > 10 ** 7 or p["N"] < 4 * p["floor"]:
        return False
    return True


WEIRD = [0, -1, -0.0, 1e-300, 1e300, np.nan, np.inf, -np.inf, True, False, "1", None, [1],
         np.float32(0.5), np.int64(7), np.complex128(1 + 0j), 1j, np.float64(2.0), 0.5, 1, 2, 3.5]
GOOD_DT = [0.1, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025, 0.002, 0.001, 0.0005, 0.0002, 0.0001]


def fuzz_check(rng):
    for _ in range(n(20000)):
        p = dict(model.SET_I)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:                       # random but mostly valid
            p.update(N=int(rng.integers(1, 3000)), floor=int(rng.integers(1, 50)),
                     dt=float(rng.choice(GOOD_DT + [0.03, 0.3, 1.0, 0.0001 / 2, 1 / 3])),
                     tick=float(10 ** rng.uniform(-13, 0.1)), s=float(rng.uniform(0, 1.2)))
        for _ in range(int(rng.integers(0, 3))):
            k = str(rng.choice(list(model.SETTINGS)))
            p[k] = WEIRD[int(rng.integers(len(WEIRD)))]

        if r < 0.03:
            p.pop(str(rng.choice(list(p))))
        elif r < 0.06:
            p["extra"] = 1
        expect = oracle_check(p)
        kind, val = outcome(model.check, p)
        if kind not in ("ok", "ValueError"):
            record("model.check raises only ValueError on bad settings", False, (p, kind, val))
            continue
        record("model.check raises only ValueError on bad settings", True)
        record("model.check accepts exactly the valid settings", (kind == "ok") == expect, (p, kind, val, expect))


# ====================================================================== model.simulate
def random_settings(rng):
    p = calibrate.draw(rng, calibrate.SPX_RANGES)
    p.update(N=int(rng.choice([16, 40, 100, 500, 2000])), floor=int(rng.integers(1, 5)),
             dt=float(rng.choice([0.1, 0.05, 0.02, 0.01])), tick=float(rng.choice([0.01, 0.001, 0.0001])))
    p["N"] = max(p["N"], 4 * p["floor"])
    return p


def sim_case(args):
    seed, = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    res = []
    rec = lambda name, ok, ex=None: res.append((name, bool(ok), None if ok else repr(ex)[:600]))
    p = random_settings(rng)
    days = int(rng.integers(1, 120))
    chart = bool(rng.random() < 0.85)
    brk = None
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        lv = np.sort(rng.uniform(0.001, 0.3, 3))
        if lv[0] < lv[1] < lv[2]:
            brk = dict(levels=tuple(float(x) for x in lv), halt_minutes=float(rng.uniform(1, 390)))
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                brk["last_pause_minute"] = float(rng.uniform(0, 390))
    shocks = None
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        shocks = {int(d): float(rng.uniform(-0.5, 0.5)) for d in rng.integers(0, days, 3)}
    quiet = rng.random() < 0.1                      # no news: the value moves only on shocks
    if quiet:
        p["sigma_eps"] = 0.0
    kw = dict(seed=int(seed), chartists=chart, breakers=brk, shocks=shocks,
              max_gap=None if rng.random() < 0.2 else 1.0)
    try:
        o = model.simulate(p, days, **kw)
    except model.RunawayError as e:
        rec("simulate returns or raises RunawayError (nothing else)", True)
        rec("RunawayError.day is within the run", isinstance(e.day, int) and 1 <= e.day <= days, (e.day, days))
        return res
    except Exception as e:                          # noqa: BLE001
        rec("simulate returns or raises RunawayError (nothing else)", False,
            (p, days, kw, type(e).__name__, str(e), traceback.format_exc()[-400:]))
        return res
    rec("simulate returns or raises RunawayError (nothing else)", True)
    N, fl = p["N"], p["floor"]
    rec("series lengths are days+1 (closes) and days (returns, halts)",
        all(len(o[k]) == days + 1 for k in ("lp", "lf", "z", "x")) and len(o["r"]) == days and len(o["halts"]) == days)
    rec("everything finite", all(np.all(np.isfinite(o[k])) for k in ("lp", "lf", "z", "x", "r")), p)
    rec("starts at price = value = 1 (log 0)", o["lp"][0] == 0 and o["lf"][0] == 0)
    rec("r is the day-to-day change of log price", np.array_equal(o["r"], np.diff(o["lp"])))
    rec("same seed -> identical run", all(np.array_equal(o[k], v) for k, v in
                                           model.simulate(p, days, **kw).items()))
    nc = o["z"] * N
    rec("chartist counts are whole numbers", close(nc, np.round(nc), atol=1e-6), nc[:5])
    if chart:
        rec("floor: at least `floor` chartists and fundamentalists every day",
            np.all(np.round(nc) >= fl) and np.all(N - np.round(nc) >= fl), (N, fl, nc.min(), nc.max()))
        rec("opinion x is between -1 and 1", np.all(np.abs(o["x"]) <= 1 + 1e-12))
        npl = np.round(nc * (1 + o["x"]) / 2)
        rec("optimist counts are whole numbers", close(npl, nc * (1 + o["x"]) / 2, atol=1e-6))
    else:
        rec("no chartists: z = 0 and x = 0 all along", np.all(o["z"] == 0) and np.all(o["x"] == 0))
    rec("halts only take values 0-3", set(np.unique(o["halts"])) <= {0, 1, 2, 3})
    if brk is None:
        rec("no breakers -> no halts", np.all(o["halts"] == 0))
    else:
        fall = o["r"]
        l1, l2, l3 = (np.log(1 - x) for x in brk["levels"])
        d3 = o["halts"] == 3
        rec("a day closed by breaker level 3 closes at least that far down", np.all(fall[d3] <= l3 + 1e-12),
            (fall[d3], l3))
        if "last_pause_minute" not in brk:
            rec("an un-halted day (pauses allowed all day) closes above level 1",
                np.all(fall[o["halts"] == 0] > l1 - 1e-12), (fall[o["halts"] == 0].min(), l1))
    if quiet:
        want = np.zeros(days)
        for d, x in (shocks or {}).items():
            want[d] += np.log1p(x)
        rec("without news the value moves exactly by the policy shocks",
            close(np.diff(o["lf"]), want, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12), (np.diff(o["lf"])[:5], want[:5]))
    # the price moves in whole ticks: lp = a ln(1+tick) + b ln(1-tick) with whole a, b
    # (holds only if ln(1+tick), ln(1-tick) are not too close; checked step by step via day changes)
    return res


def sim_extra(args):
    """Exact answers: no chartists, no noise, no news -> the price never moves."""
    seed, = args
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    p = random_settings(rng)
    p.update(sigma_mu=0.0, sigma_eps=0.0)
    o = model.simulate(p, int(rng.integers(1, 60)), seed=seed, chartists=False)
    return [("no chartists, noise or news -> price and value stay exactly at 1",
             bool(np.all(o["lp"] == 0) and np.all(o["lf"] == 0)), None)]


def fuzz_simulate(pool, rng):
    for name, ok, ex in sum(pool.map(sim_case, [(int(s),) for s in rng.integers(0, 2**31, n(6000))],
                                     chunksize=20), []):
